title: A stale class or cue edit cannot silently overwrite a newer one
acceptance: PATCH /api/v1/classes/:id and PATCH /api/v1/cues/:id accept an optional precondition (for example the updatedAtMs the client last saw); when it no longer matches, the write is refused with a documented status and error code instead of applied.
Requests without the precondition behave exactly as today, so the web app and current iOS builds keep working.
The precondition and its error are in packages/shared, the OpenAPI document and api.md, with integration tests for match, mismatch and absent.
nextAction: Found on 2026-11-01 while setting iOS RF-1011's retry policy: the server applies class and cue PATCHes unconditionally, so an edit queued offline on iOS can silently overwrite a newer web edit when it replays. iOS holds edits older than 7 days for review as a stopgap. Contract change: land here first, then refresh the iOS snapshots and send the precondition from the iOS outbox. Agent-created: Backlog until the owner sets Ready.

evidence.summary: PATCH /cues/:id updates by id with no version or timestamp check (classes.ts PATCH /:id is the same).
iOS RF-1011 owner decisions, including the 7-day hold that this task would make unnecessary.
